subject: middle children
one_liner: A 412-store coffeehouse chain that seats you between two other parties and prints a name on your cup that is close to yours.
brand_voice_notes: Retail-corporate sincerity with the affection removed. Mezz talks about being overlooked the way a chain talks about sourcing: proudly, in the passive voice, with a footnote. Every promise is a slight. Nothing is ever acknowledged as a slight. Store numbering, birth-order language and family-photo references are used as if they were ordinary operational terms. Never wink, never soften, never apologize.

hero.sub: Mezz is a coffeehouse for the second of three. We seat you between two louder parties, print a name within two characters of yours, and do not ask how you have been in a way that requires an answer.

features.title: Birth-Order Queueing
features.blurb: Orders are sequenced against documented birth order, imported from your family group chat. Firstborns are made first because they always were. The youngest is made next because the youngest is still the youngest. Yours comes out at a sensible point after that, warm enough.

features.title: Approximate Name Capture
features.blurb: The cup printer renders a name within two characters of the one you gave. Internal research found that correcting a barista was the longest conversation 61% of our members had that week, so the opportunity is preserved at every store.

features.title: Table Topology
features.blurb: Every Mezz floor plan is certified middle-seat-only. No corner two-tops, no window banquette, no stool at the end of the bar. You are seated between a first date and a man on speakerphone, which is where you were going to sit anyway.

demo_screen_concept: The Mezz Store Console for Store No. 2 of 3: a live CSS floor plan where every seat is a middle seat and only the middles are selectable, each one flanked by two auto-assigned neighbouring parties with a name, an activity and a decibel rating; a cup-name field that garbles whatever you type into an approximate name in real time as you type it; and a queue rail showing your position sliding downward every few seconds as firstborns are inserted ahead of you, with a running note on why.

images.rationale: Hero skipped because the direction is a two-ink typographic riso zine and the hero is a knocked-out doubled headline plus a pure-CSS cup diagram; a photo would break the two-ink rule. Demo assets skipped because the demo screen is a floor plan, a queue rail and a text field, none of which are photo-shaped. Whole budget went to the three testimonial headshots, art-directed as riso duotone portraits in the page's own two inks so they read as printed on the same sheet.

design_direction.style: Risograph two-ink print, newsprint daylight mode. The page is staged as a short-run zine pulled on a duplicator by a 412-store coffee chain that could afford proper printing and chose this instead. Exactly two inks exist on the whole page: federal blue #0B49C8 and fluorescent pink #FF4FA3, laid on uncoated newsprint #F1ECDF, with a near-black #141414 reserved for body text only. No shadows anywhere, because a drum press cannot print a shadow; depth is carried entirely by misregistration, which is the organising move. Every display element is printed twice, the pink layer offset 3 to 5px up and left of the blue layer, so headlines, rules and the logotype all read slightly out of register, like the sheet shifted in the drum. Where the two inks cross they overprint via mix-blend-mode: multiply into a bruised violet, never a third named colour. Texture is a coarse halftone built in pure CSS: a repeating-radial-gradient dot screen at 3px pitch, opacity 0.10 to 0.18, laid over every ink fill so no area of colour is ever flat. Paper grain is a fixed, non-animated speckle from two offset repeating-linear-gradients at 1.5% opacity across the whole body. Nothing has a border radius above 2px and every keyline is a hard 2px or 3px ink rule, never a hairline and never grey. The second motif is the knockout: section headers are cut out of a solid ink block in the paper colour, the way a riso does reversed type, always uppercase, always tight. The third is the registration mark, a 14px crosshair in a 999px circle printed in both inks 3px apart, used as the list bullet, the feature index, the price-tier mark and the section seam marker. Section seams are a 10px band of 45-degree pink hatch with a gap cut where the section number sits. No glass, no blur, no clay, no bento lattice, no foil, no banknote plate, no sprocket rail, no drafting grid, no wall label, no film frame, no moulded shell, no vellum rule.
design_direction.archetype: Retail coffeehouse chain product page issued as a two-ink risograph zine, with store numbering and a membership tier table
design_direction.motion_vocab: Paper-feed jolts. Nothing eases in or out; interactive elements snap their pink layer 2 to 3px on hover, as if the sheet shifted mid-pull, using steps(1) or a 90ms linear transition and nothing slower. Misregistration widens on hover and closes on active, so pressing something looks like the registration finally landing. No fades, no scale, no parallax, no scroll-triggered reveals. All of it is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, where the offsets go static.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Full-bleed newsprint. Top strip is a printer's slug: MEZZ COFFEE CO. on the left, STORE No. 2 OF 3 and a run count on the right, in 11px uppercase blue with 0.18em tracking, hemmed by a 3px blue rule. The h1 sits enormous and flush-left at clamp(3.2rem, 11vw, 8.5rem), Archivo Black, line-height 0.86, printed twice: a pink copy offset -4px/-4px behind a blue copy, so it reads doubled at a glance. Sub-copy is capped at 46ch directly beneath, near-black. The CTA is a solid blue block with knocked-out paper-colour type and a pink shadow-layer offset 4px down and right, no radius. To the right on desktop sits a pure-CSS riso cup diagram: three stacked ink circles in a vertical column, the top and bottom at 92px in blue, the middle one at 62px in pink and inset from the column axis, with a registration crosshair over the middle circle and a hand-set caption reading YOU ARE THE MIDDLE ONE. Below the fold line, three registration marks and a hatch seam introduce section 01.
